## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Set `updatedAt` explicitly instead of relying on an empty `updateMany`

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1024
- packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400-405

Explanation:
`updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. It relies on Prisma's `@updatedAt` to bump the timestamp, but Prisma may treat an empty update as a no-op. If it does, `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` never changes.

There are four further problems:
- **Extra writes on every webhook.** This runs an unconditional write on every webhook-driven refresh. It covers all of the credential's selected calendars, not just those in `parsedArgs`.
- **New failure path.** If the write throws, `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` fails even though the cache was already written.
- **Nothing reads the value.** The UI's `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, not from `SelectedCalendar`.
- **Wrong parameter type.** The helper is typed as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which allows relation operations. `updateMany` does not accept those; the correct type is `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

Fix: either remove the call, or set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly and wrap the call in try/catch. In both cases, correct the parameter type.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
static async updateManyByCredentialId(
  credentialId: number,
  data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput
) {
  return prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data });
}

// CalendarService
try {
  await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, { updatedAt: new Date() });
} catch (e) {
  log.error("Failed to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt", e);
}
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Throw `TRPCError` instead of a plain `Error` in `deleteCacheHandler`

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-30

Explanation:
A plain `Error` reaches the client as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) and is logged as a server fault. A missing credential, or one the user cannot access, should return `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN` instead. That lets clients and monitoring tell these cases apart from real crashes.

The handler also calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly instead of going through `CalendarCacheRepository`. This makes it harder to test with the repository mock.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";
import { CalendarCacheRepository } from "@calcom/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository";
...
if (!credential) {
  throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found" });
}
await new CalendarCacheRepository().deleteManyByCredential(credentialId);
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Hide "Delete cached data" for credentials the handler will always reject

Affected:
- packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:67-73
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-22

Explanation:
`hasCache` ignores both `delegationCredentialId` and `disableConnectionModification`. However, `deleteCacheHandler` only accepts credentials where `userId === user.id`.

As a result:
- **Delegation and team credentials** (team credentials have `userId` null) show a destructive action that always fails with an error toast.
- **Contexts with `disableConnectionModification`** still let users change credential state.

Fix: either hide the action for these credentials, or extend the handler's authorization to cover team and delegation credentials.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const hasCache =
  isGoogleCalendar && !!cacheUpdatedAt && !delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification;
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Add tests for deleteCache authorization and connectedCalendars enrichment

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:13-33
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-36
- packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-188

Explanation:
This change adds a destructive, authorization-gated mutation and changes the `connectedCalendars` response shape, but includes no tests. The following cases need coverage:

- **deleteCache, other user's credential:** the call is rejected and no rows are deleted.
- **deleteCache, own credential:** only that credential's cache rows are removed.
- **getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, multiple rows:** returns the max `updatedAt` per credential.
- **getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, empty input:** handles an empty `credentialIds` array.
- **connectedCalendars:** sets `cacheUpdatedAt: null` for credentials with no cache rows.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
it("rejects deleting cache for a credential owned by another user", async () => {
  await expect(deleteCacheHandler({ ctx: { user: otherUser }, input: { credentialId } })).rejects.toThrow();
  expect(await prisma.calendarCache.count({ where: { credentialId } })).toBe(2);
});
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Format the cache timestamp with the user's locale instead of hardcoded en-US

Affected:
- packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88-94

Explanation:
`new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's language, so a translated label is followed by a US-formatted date. It also uses the browser timezone rather than the profile timezone.

Separately, the "Cache Status" info row is a clickable `DropdownMenuItem`. Selecting it does nothing except close the menu.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const { t, i18n } = useLocale();
...
timestamp: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(i18n.language, { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)),
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Make the webhook helper script portable and return correct exit codes

Affected:
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:4-8
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:11-18
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:56-59
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:67-71

Explanation:
- **`sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only.** GNU sed treats `''` as the script, so the `.env` update fails on Linux.
- **`ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the current working directory,** so the script can create or modify the wrong file.
- **`cleanup` always exits 0,** so the rate-limit and missing-URL failure paths report success.
- **`TM_KEYWORD` contains a greedy `.*`.** The match can capture extra characters, which are then written unescaped into the sed replacement.
- **`/tmp/tmole.log` is a fixed, predictable path.** This is unsafe on shared hosts.
- **`pgrep` can return multiple PIDs,** which the script then treats as a single value.

Proposed fix:
~~~bash
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env"
TM_KEYWORD='https://[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\.tunnelmole\.net'
cleanup() { local code=${1:-0}; ...; exit "$code"; }
# on failures: cleanup 1
tmp="$(mktemp)"; grep -v '^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=' "$ENV_FILE" > "$tmp"; echo "GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL" >> "$tmp"; mv "$tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Security
Consensus: 2/3 reviewers
Title: Add `tsx` as a pinned dev dependency instead of resolving it via `npx`

Affected:
- apps/web/package.json:11

Explanation:
If `tsx` is not installed, `npx tsx` downloads and runs whatever version is latest at that moment. That makes `dev:cron` non-reproducible and dependent on the network. It is also an unpinned supply-chain execution path.

Proposed fix:
~~~json
"dev:cron": "tsx cron-tester.ts"
~~~
Also add a pinned `tsx` to `devDependencies`.

## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Confirm intent of hiding "Remove App" for errored credentials when `disableConnectionModification` is set

Affected:
- packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:123-132

Explanation:
The second `actions` block (credentials without calendars, typically ones with errors) previously checked only `delegationCredentialId`. It now also passes `disableConnectionModification`. When that flag is set, users can no longer remove a broken credential. Confirm this behavior change is intended; otherwise pass `false` here to keep the old behavior.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
<CredentialActionsDropdown
  ...
  disableConnectionModification={false}
/>
~~~

## 9) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Avoid stamping existing cache rows with the migration time

Affected:
- packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:1-9

Explanation:
`DEFAULT NOW()` sets every existing `CalendarCache` row to the migration time. The UI will then show "Last updated: <deploy time>" for caches that may be much older.

The header comment also says the column is added "without a default value", which contradicts the SQL below it.

Fix: backfill a more accurate value and correct the comment.

Proposed fix:
~~~sql
ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();
-- optionally: UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - INTERVAL '<CACHE_TTL>';
~~~

## 10) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Respect the calendar-cache feature flag and skip the query when there are no credentials

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29

Explanation:
The handler always creates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository`. This bypasses the disabled-feature mock, so it queries the cache even when caching is off. It also runs a `groupBy` query when `credentialIds` is empty.

Fix: use the existing feature-aware factory and short-circuit when the list is empty.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const cacheStatuses = credentialIds.length
  ? await cacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds) // obtained via feature-aware factory
  : [];
~~~
